answer: An operator that moves capital between 180 aliases as a result destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. Because the vault forfeiture is applied at exit, the ledge ledger totals each burn, and the knoll audit records the amount lost per key. Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 80% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned which means nobody profits from it. That is 11 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
